exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal birth vs. cesarean delivery prior to the second stage of labor)
outcome: Pelvic floor function (POPQ, perineal ultrasound, Paper Towel Test, Incontinence Severity Index, Pelvic Floor Impact Questionnaire, Wexner Fecal Incontinence Scale, Female Sexual Function Index)
cohort: Nulliparous women (336 vaginal birth, 138 cesarean delivery) recruited during pregnancy or immediately postpartum
finding: Vaginal birth resulted in more changes in pelvic organ prolapse and objective urinary incontinence, but no increase in self-reported pelvic floor dysfunction at 6 months postpartum compared to cesarean delivery prior to the second stage of labor.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth resulted in greater prolapse changes and objective urinary incontinence compared with cesarean delivery before the second stage of labor.
